pr_title: [Settings UI] Represent Cursor Height as a slider
pr_body:
Change the vintage cursor height number box to a slider.

## References
Related:  #9370

## PR Checklist
* [x] Closes #9377
* [x] zadjii-msft edit: Now _this one_ closes #9175
* [x] CLA signed. If not, go over [here](https://cla.opensource.microsoft.com/microsoft/Terminal) and sign the CLA
* [x] Schema updated.
* [x] Documentation updated here: MicrosoftDocs/terminal#278 

## Detailed Description of the Pull Request / Additional comments

It seems like the cursor height couldn't be lower than 25 percent regardless of the given value, so I've changed the `MinCursorHeightPercent` in CustomTextRenderer header file.

## Validation Steps Performed
Manual validation

Hello @carlos-zamora!

Because this pull request has the `AutoMerge` label, I will be glad to assist with helping to merge this pull request once all check-in policies pass.

##### p.s. you can customize the way I help with merging this pull request, such as holding this pull request until a specific person approves. Simply @mention me (`@msftbot`) and give me an instruction to get started! Learn more [here](https://github.com/microsoft/fluentui/wiki/Advanced-auto-merge).

The GdiEngine is the one that's used for drawing the vintage console host (conhost.exe). The DxEngine is only used by the Terminal. He was just asking to make sure that this change was only scoped to the DxEngine, so that the vintage console host didn't change behavior. We can't change the console as easily as we can the Terminal ☺️

> Sorry for commenting in closed PR, but I don't think it worth creating a new issue.
> 
> > Please don't update the GdiEngine for this. Update only the DxEngine one.
> 
> @miniksa could you please explain a little more about the GdiEngine and why one shouldn't update it along with the DxEngine? I've read the [How are the Windows graphics/messaging stack assembled?](https://github.com/microsoft/terminal/blob/main/doc/Niksa.md?rgh-link-date=2021-03-09T20%3A36%3A54Z#gfxMsgStack) section (great explanation, by the way!) but still can't find an answer.

Couple things:
- The `GdiEngine` is only used for the `conhost.exe`/`OpenConsole.exe` product, also known as the inbox windows console, for its headed window implementation. The Windows Terminal product, by contrast, uses `DxEngine` instead. Given this PR is coming in from the perspective of the Terminal settings UI, I thought it appropriate to scope it to the Terminal rendering targets only.
- Scoping to only Terminal, and not the inbox console, drops a lot of potential compatibility and OS interaction concerns off my mind. For instance, there could be some interaction I'm not foreseeing with the property sheet (`console.dll`) or the conhost settings processing that could cause a bug. It could be that someone out there is using a regkey with a size of 12% for their cursor implementation on a factory line, but because it always bottomed out graphically at 25% for the GDI renderer, it was never a problem. In a perfect world, our code base would have checked the 25% minimum in the propsheet, console settings code, and at the renderer, but it's highly possible and even probable that this is the only check. 
- Our long term goal is that no one will use the classic console window and by extension the `GdiEngine` anymore once Terminal can completely replace it. Or at least replace the graphical and interaction components as ConPTY will still need to be there no matter what. So I'd rather not spend effort on it and avoid potential unpredictable future bug investigations by just... not changing it if we don't NEED to.
Thanks! Now it became clear to me 😊

# Description of the new feature/enhancement

Allow "vintage" cursor to have values lower than 25, it is presently capped between 25 to 100.  I just want to have the capability of setting it to a smaller value that is larger than `underline`

<!--

Remove the bottom limit and allow floating point values.
comments:
The vintage cursor is intended to provide compatibility with folks' expectations of the windows console. It's not meant to be a good fun and expressive cursor for people to personalize with. What specifically are you looking for? Why do you want this capability?

> and allow floating point values

So, you want a cursor with a fractional percentage height? I'm gonna say _no_ to that one.
Well can you at least make it allow 1-24?
I guess I don't see why not

![vintage](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/23057110/109766102-b1e85580-7c30-11eb-913f-e0e6f28d9ebb.gif)

Windows Terminal Preview v1.7.572.0

allowed input range may be too large
Mmmm nope, this _wasn't_ closed by #9370. We still need to update `_drawCursor` in `CustomTextRenderer.cpp` to allow `MinCursorHeightPercent` to be `1`

review_comments:
@carlos-zamora, @zadjii-msft what if we restrict the minimum cursor height value to 1px? On values less than 25 the cursor is getting smaller until it reaches the 1px height. If one decreases the value further, it won't change anything. 

If you think it's ok, I'll also update the docs.
